title: Electronic Music Pioneer Suzanne Ciani, 80, Finds an Audience at Last
summary:
Suzanne Ciani is 80 years old, and she helped shape electronic music. Electronic music is made with machines such as synthesizers instead of only regular instruments like guitars or drums.

Ciani was born in Ohio and studied music composition at UC Berkeley. There she met Don Buchla, who designed synthesizers, and she became one of the first people to master his Buchla modular analog synthesizer.

In 1974 she founded a company called Ciani/Musica. It made sounds for brands such as AT&T, General Electric and Coca-Cola. She created the soda's "pop & pour" sound logo and the Columbia Pictures intro score. She has released more than 25 studio and live albums and has five Grammy nominations, all in the new age category.

Ciani told Billboard that when she was starting out, she was excited about electronic music and thought the whole world would be too. Instead, she says, she ran into a wall, because nobody knew what the machine was or where the sound was coming from. "I had no audience then. Now I have an audience," she said. "The kids know what's going on. They have the machines."

Today she is playing live shows. This weekend she performs her first concert in Scotland, at the Sonica Festival in Glasgow. In early November she will play Atomika, a new science and music festival in the desert outside Roswell, New Mexico. She is also selling her house after 34 years because she wants a new chapter. She says the basis of technology is change.
why_it_matters: Ciani's story shows how a new kind of music and technology can start small, take years to be understood, and later inspire many young people.
